items.title: Ask HN: Where is the merit in AI-era?
items.summary: Society was partly built on rewarding a subtle mix of talent and effort and this feels slippery now. I see a lot of content being generated: some cool things, but many vibe-coded in one evening and forgotten the next day. In math, the Riemann hypothesis was just proved with AI, in a proof no human can read yet. The notion of merit we were holding is drowning in noise. Where do you see merit moving? items.title: Ask HN: Where are all the amazing AI-generated software?
items.summary: I feel like the most amazing thing about AI so far is AI itself. Is anyone using a brand-new tool that was not available 5 years ago? I see people decompiling/reverse engineering the Adobe suite, which is an amazing feat, but the resulting software itself is barely usable. Since it’s so easy to build anything now, I get a sense we’re seeing a proliferation of one-off, proof-of-concept projects, where great software takes time and effort and often multiple people, AI notwithstanding.
